# Results — Study 183 (Fisher-Transform) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Ehlers' Fisher Transform
maps the close into a Gaussian via atanh on the clamped normalised midpoint of the
rolling high-low range; the signal is the Fisher/Trigger (Fisher-lagged-1) crossover.
Tested on six liquid daily tapes (SPY, QQQ, IWM, AAPL, TSLA, NVDA), 10-year window,
5-day fixed-horizon forward-return backtest, pinned against a random-direction control
on the same entries. As-of **2026-06-15**. Trades pooled across tickers: **n = 8,329**.*

## Monotonicity proof — the transform adds zero information

| Ticker | Fisher entries | Raw-x entries | Fisher-in-raw | Raw-in-Fisher |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 1,389 | 1,389 | **1.0000** | **1.0000** |
| QQQ  | 1,396 | 1,396 | **1.0000** | **1.0000** |
| IWM  | 1,408 | 1,408 | **1.0000** | **1.0000** |
| AAPL | 1,370 | 1,370 | **1.0000** | **1.0000** |
| TSLA | 1,378 | 1,378 | **1.0000** | **1.0000** |
| NVDA | 1,389 | 1,389 | **1.0000** | **1.0000** |

The Fisher Transform is strictly monotone in the clamped normalised price `raw_x`, so
replacing Fisher with `raw_x` produces **identical crossover timestamps** on every tape.
The transform adds zero signal information beyond what the underlying price extremes
already contain — confirmed empirically at 100% agreement on 10 years of real data.

## Primary signal: Fisher/Trigger crossover, 5-day forward return

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Fisher crossover (signal)** | 8,329 | **49.2%** | **-2.59** | **-0.93** |
| Random direction (control)    | 8,329 | 48.9%     | -5.49    | -1.02    |

- The Fisher crossover's gross expectancy is **-2.59 bps/trade** at HAC *t* = **-0.93** —
  statistically **indistinguishable from zero** (and if anything slightly negative).
- It does **not beat the coin**: the signal arm (-2.59 bps) is *better* than the random
  control (-5.49 bps), but both are noise — neither has a meaningful directional edge.

No instrument carries a signal: every HAC |*t*| < 1.3. TSLA's positive mean (+5.34 bps)
is noise-level (*t* = 0.45) and is not robust across holding periods.

## Holding-period sweep (pooled, gross)

| Hold (days) | n | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1  | 8,329 | -4.72 | **-2.29** |
| 3  | 8,329 | -3.21 | -1.29 |
| 5  | 8,329 | -2.59 | -0.93 |
| 10 | 8,329 | -5.82 | **-1.96** |
| 20 | 8,329 | -8.98 | **-2.43** |

At 1-day and 20-day horizons the signal is a **statistically significant loser** (*t* < -2),
consistent with short-term momentum (the signal fires in the wrong direction at 1-day) and
mean-reversion at longer windows. There is no holding period where the signal is profitable.

## Cost sweep (5-day hold, net)

| Round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | -2.59 | -0.93 |
| 0.5 bps         | -3.09 | -1.11 |
| 1.0 bps         | -3.59 | -1.29 |
| 2.0 bps         | -4.59 | -1.65 |
| 5.0 bps         | -7.59 | **-2.72** |

Because the gross edge is already negative, there is **no positive break-even cost**.
Every basis point of trading cost simply deepens the already-negative expectancy.

## Synthetic positive control — the machine works when there is something to find

The Fisher crossover is a *momentum follower* (it fires when price shifts strongly through
the look-back range), not a mean-reversion signal. On a synthetic tape with planted
momentum (negative AR(1) mean_rev), the signal beats a coin. On a martingale it is a fair
die. On a strongly mean-reverting tape it is *on the wrong side* and loses to the coin.
This confirms the engine is a faithful structure detector — the real-tape verdict is a
statement about the market (daily equity markets do not exhibit the kind of persistent
short-horizon momentum the Fisher crossover needs), not the machinery.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Gross HAC *t* = -0.93 at 5-day hold; no instrument |*t*| > 1.3;
  monotonicity proof shows the atanh transform adds zero information beyond price extremes.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Negative gross expectancy at every tested holding period; a
  significant loser at 1-day (*t* = -2.29) and 20-day (*t* = -2.43) horizons. Costs
  compound a pre-existing loss.
- **The transform is monotone — CONFIRMED.** Fisher and raw-x crossovers are identical on
  100% of entry bars across all six tickers. The Gaussian normalisation changes the
  *scale* of the indicator values but not the *ordering* — and it is the ordering that
  generates the crossover timestamps. The transform is pure presentation.
